title: Why the Sun Shouldn't Burn
hook: Part one: the Sun's core is actually too cold to shine.
script: Part one: the Sun's core is actually too cold to shine. At 15 million degrees, how do protons ever cross the Coulomb barrier? Every rule of classical physics says their positive charges must push them apart. They only fuse because quantum tunnelling lets them slip through that wall. The odds are so low that a single proton waits billions of years. Without that loophole, no stars exist. If stars burned by simple heat alone, would life have ever had time to evolve? Follow for part two.

Classical physics says the sun should be completely dark.
A quantum loophole is the only reason sunlight reaches Earth.
